name: immunodeficiency overview
title: Immunodeficiency decision chart: recurrent infections beyond what is expected for age (10 warning signs) sorted by the pattern of infection into phagocyte (chronic granulomatous disease), complement, T cell (SCID) and B cell (selective IgA deficiency, CVID) defects, or a secondary immunodeficiency from drugs, cancer, HIV or other illness, each with its clues, key disease, test and treatment

root.title: Recurrent infections: MORE than expected for the AGE? Then WHICH ARM of immunity is broken?
lines: suspect it with 2 or more of the 10 WARNING SIGNS · child: ≥ 4 ear infections or ≥ 2 pneumonias in a year · adult: ≥ 2 ear or sinus infections in a year
both ages: deep abscesses · persistent thrush · needing IV antibiotics · failure to thrive / chronic diarrhea · family history

groups.title: PRIMARY (germline): the PATTERN of infection points to the arm
lines: WHAT bugs, and from WHAT AGE?

head: h
Phagocyte defect
the commonest primary INNATE defect
dx: • NADPH oxidase defect: ingested bugs survive

head: h
Complement defect
any age
dx: • EARLY: milder encapsulated infections, the MOST autoimmunity
• the MOST SEVERE: RECURRENT systemic Neisseria

head: h
T cell defect
the MOST SEVERE
pres: • mycobacteria, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr, varicella, Candida, Pneumocystis
• failure to thrive, thrush, severe eczema
• graft-vs-host from mother's T cells · infection after BCG vaccine
dx: low or absent TRECs (T-cell receptor excision circles)

head: h
B cell (antibody) defect
after maternal IgG WANES, or in adults
pres: • H. influenzae, pneumococcus, strep · Giardia, enterovirus
dx: • IgG REPLACEMENT: monthly IV or weekly subcutaneous

head: h
Secondary immunodeficiency
acquired
dx: • antibiotics for each fever, sore throat
